competency_fulfillment.rationale: Of the thirteen samples, only six actually involve a pictorial model: the base-10 block items in seeds 42, 43, 45, and 46, and the block-building items in seeds 51 and 501; the other seven, seeds 44, 50, 53, 500, 502, 600, and 601, are pure word-form-to-numeral conversions like seed 44's "Write 596 in words.", which never render or reference any pictorial model at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Where pictorial representation is tested, both directions of the skill appear: reading a pictorial model into a numeral, as in seed 42's "What number do the blocks show?", and building a pictorial model from a numeral, as in seed 51's "Use base-10 blocks to show the number 8229."

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The numbers used in the pictorial items, 410, 4688, 8229, 5795, 6844, and 6554, and the block-reading format match Grade 3 Quarter 1 place-value work without introducing later-grade notation.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The pictorial subset varies between multiple-choice block reading in seeds 42, 43, 45, and 46, and open block-building in seeds 51 and 501, giving two distinct interaction styles for the represented skill.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty in this node is partly driven by whether a sample tests word-to-numeral literacy versus pictorial-model reading, two different underlying skills rather than one competency scaled by difficulty; seeds 600 and 601 in this node are identical in question text and correct answer to seeds 600 and 601 in sibling node mat_g3_na_q1_1, whose stated competency is reading and writing numerals and words rather than pictorial representation.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every rendered number stays at or below 9630, as in seed 500's "The number 9630 is written in words as 'nine thousand six hundred twenty'. True or False?", respecting the competency's stated "up to 10 000" ceiling.
